title: Qrich1 perturbation lowers a Scn2b/Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b module in thalamic and brainstem/midbrain neurons
exact_observed_result: Qrich1 perturbation yielded 75 FDR genes in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, led by Scn2b logFC -1.277 FDR 6.86e-37, Celf3 -1.353 FDR 1.24e-30, Ldhd -1.981 FDR 3.67e-22, and Map1a -0.686 FDR 2.58e-08. 155 MB Glut and 191 MB P MY GABA reproduced the Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b or Celf3/Map1a/Ldhd down-regulated core at smaller breadth.
biological_interpretation: A broadly expressed nucleoplasmic QRICH1 target produces a sharply biased neuronal expression module centered on thalamic and caudal populations, with recurrent repression of ion-channel, RNA-binding, and metabolic genes rather than a uniform brain-wide knockdown state.
caveats: Eleven profiled classes had no FDR-level Qrich1 downstream row, so the claim is state-selective rather than pan-neuronal.

prior_expectation.summary: QRICH1 is broadly detected and nucleoplasmic in the Human Protein Atlas; that broad expression makes the focused thalamic/midbrain Scn2b/Celf3/Ldhd/Tlcd3b response an unexpected cell-context refinement.

citations.supports: broad QRICH1 RNA and low brain-region specificity
